questions.scenario: A beginner is setting up an email account for the first time.
questions.hint: Avoid using simple number sequences or common words that anyone, even a total stranger, could guess on their first try.

candidates.explanation: Stringing random, everyday words together is easy for you to remember but very long and difficult for a hacker to guess.
A completely random mix of letters, numbers, and symbols is incredibly hard for someone to guess, though it can be hard to remember.
This is one of the most guessed passwords in the world. Anyone trying to break into your account will try this first.
Using unrelated words makes a password long, which is the best way to keep your account safe.

questions.scenario: A user is creating a password for a new online shopping website.
questions.hint: Avoid using the name of the website you are on, even if you add a year or an exclamation mark at the end.

candidates.explanation: Using a combination of unrelated words avoids easy guesses and provides a high level of protection.
Using random characters without any real words or predictable patterns keeps your account highly secure.
Combining a long phrase of random words with a number significantly increases how long it would take someone to guess it.
Hackers know this trick! If they see you are on a shopping site, their automated programs will immediately guess the website's name plus the current year.

questions.scenario: Someone is trying to make a 'clever' password by swapping letters for symbols (like using @ for the letter 'a').
questions.hint: Replacing letters with similar-looking symbols doesn't fool the automated programs that hackers use to break into accounts.

candidates.explanation: True randomness with no real words inside of it is far superior to trying to make a real word look 'complex'.
Swapping 'a' for '@' and 'o' for '0' is an old trick. Hackers program their tools to automatically check for these exact symbol swaps, making it very easy to crack.
Length is your best friend. A long phrase of normal words is actually much stronger than a short word stuffed with tricky symbols.
Three completely random words are easy for you to picture in your head but almost impossible for a computer program to guess.
